narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts that you have a 56% chance of not passing your final year. Because this probability is above the threshold set by the school, you are required to take additional remedial courses to help support your learning and improve your chances of success.

The most important factor influencing this prediction is your current lack of intention to pursue higher education after graduation. In your school, every other student who is not required to take remedial courses has expressed a desire to continue their studies, making your situation quite different. This lack of future academic plans strongly contributed to the model’s decision, as students with similar intentions have historically been more likely to struggle in their final year.

On the other hand, your record of not having failed any classes in the past actually worked in your favor, helping to lower your risk compared to students who have experienced previous failures. This positive aspect suggests you have demonstrated the ability to keep up with your studies so far.

Another factor that slightly reduced your risk was your daily travel time to school. Although your commute is longer than most students—between 30 and 60 minutes, while the majority travel less than 15 minutes—this did not significantly increase your risk and, in fact, had a small positive influence.

Given these factors, taking remedial courses is intended as a supportive measure. Engaging fully with these courses and considering your future educational goals can help you strengthen your academic performance and open up more opportunities after graduation.
